events.title: Star Wars Premieres in U.S. Theaters
events.description: George Lucas's space opera Star Wars (later retitled Episode IV: A New Hope) opened in a limited number of theaters in the United States on May 25, 1977, and quickly became a runaway success.
events.significance: The film revolutionized special effects and blockbuster filmmaking, launched one of the highest-grossing media franchises in history, and reshaped merchandising and popular culture.

events.title: Kennedy Announces the Moon Landing Goal
events.description: In a special address to a joint session of Congress, President John F. Kennedy declared that the United States should commit to landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to Earth before the end of the decade.
events.significance: The speech galvanized the Apollo program during the Cold War space race and led to the Moon landing of Apollo 11 in July 1969.

events.title: Scopes Trial Underway in Tennessee Following Arrest of John Scopes
events.description: In the spring of 1925, high school teacher John T. Scopes was charged with violating Tennessee's Butler Act, which banned teaching human evolution in public schools. The trial in Dayton, Tennessee, began in July 1925 and drew national attention.
events.significance: The case became a landmark clash between science and religious fundamentalism and shaped later debates over evolution education and the separation of church and state.

events.title: Death of George Floyd in Minneapolis
events.description: George Floyd, a 46-year-old Black man, died on May 25, 2020, after Minneapolis police officer Derek Chauvin knelt on his neck for more than nine minutes during an arrest. Video of the incident spread widely.
events.significance: His death sparked worldwide protests against racism and police brutality, intensified the Black Lives Matter movement, and prompted policing reform debates and the conviction of Chauvin in 2021.

events.title: Oscar Wilde Sentenced to Two Years' Hard Labour
events.description: On May 25, 1895, Irish writer and playwright Oscar Wilde was found guilty of gross indecency and sentenced to two years of hard labour in prison.
events.significance: The trial destroyed Wilde's career and health, and it later became a defining example of the persecution of homosexuality in Victorian Britain, inspiring works such as The Ballad of Reading Gaol.
